contract_plain_english: Every bounded real random variable is sub-gaussian, and its ψ₂ norm is at most its infinity norm divided by √(ln 2).

source_evidence.observation: The source defines the sub-gaussian norm by ‖X‖ψ₂ = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.
The source states that any bounded random variable X is sub-gaussian.
The source gives the one-sided estimate ‖X‖ψ₂ ≤ C‖X‖∞.
The source specifies the constant exactly as C = 1/√(ln 2).

binders: An arbitrary bounded real-valued random variable X.
conclusions: X is a sub-gaussian random variable.
Its sub-gaussian norm satisfies ‖X‖ψ₂ ≤ C‖X‖∞, equivalently ‖X‖ψ₂ ≤ ‖X‖∞/√(ln 2).
definitions_and_conventions: The sub-gaussian norm is ‖X‖ψ₂ = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.
The infinity norm ‖X‖∞ expresses the size bound on X.
The coefficient in Equation (2.17) is exactly C = 1/√(ln 2).
The notation ln denotes the natural logarithm.
hypotheses: X is bounded, so its infinity norm ‖X‖∞ is finite.
implicit_context: X is defined on an underlying probability space, and E denotes expectation on that space.
No centering, symmetry, independence, or special distributional form is required.
The same threshold 2 from Definition 2.5.6 governs the ψ₂ norm.

details: The claim applies to every bounded real random variable.
No mean-zero, symmetry, independence, or named-distribution assumption is imposed.
The ψ₂ norm uses the exponential-square scale infimum with threshold 2.
The conclusion compares the ψ₂ norm to the infinity norm.
The comparison is a one-sided non-strict upper bound, not an equality.
The constant is not merely an unspecified absolute constant in this example.

undebatable_constraints: The quantified object must be an arbitrary bounded real random variable X.
The conclusion must include that X is sub-gaussian.
The inequality direction must be ‖X‖ψ₂ ≤ C‖X‖∞.
The ψ₂ norm must retain the definition inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.
The conclusion is an upper bound, not an equality.
No mean-zero, symmetry, independence, or special-distribution hypothesis may be added.
